business_problem: CJWC wanted to reduce the extensive human effort required for strategic planning, content analysis, and other organizational tasks while preserving the integrity of human decision-making.
solution_summary: The Canadian Joint Warfare Centre implemented public Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) as a controlled, human-supervised assistant for internal organizational work rather than as a standalone decision system. CJWC applied the technology task by task, introducing it separately into activities such as strategic planning, strategic foresight, content analysis, and the development of AI policy and training materials. The operating model emphasized a controlled environment, immediate feedback, and experience-based refinement: staff used public content and reports as source material, reviewed GenAI outputs with human judgment, and iteratively adjusted usage based on real-world experience. The source does not name a specific vendor platform, storage layer, or systems integration stack, but it clearly describes an implementation pattern in which public GenAI tools support analysis and drafting while humans remain accountable for decisions, governance, and safe-use practices.

solution_components.name: public Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI)
solution_components.role: Used as a collaborative assistant for strategic planning, content analysis, and drafting or refining policy and training materials.

data_flow: CJWC staff feed individual organizational tasks plus public content and reports into public GenAI tools in a controlled environment. The model produces summaries, foresight support, and draft material that humans review and adapt, and immediate feedback from real-time use is applied iteratively to improve later planning, analysis, policy, and training work.
integration_points: CJWC strategic planning and strategic foresight workflows
CJWC AI policy and training plan
business_outcome: CJWC reports that GenAI improved strategic foresight support, made large-scale content review and summarization more efficient, saved time, freed human resources for other work, and helped refine the unit's AI policy and training approach while reinforcing safe and responsible AI use.
architecture_clues: Task-by-task implementation in a controlled environment
Immediate feedback and real-time data were used to refine effectiveness
Human expertise remained in the loop for judgment and decision-making
